newsitem.title: GERMANY: Brazil tax bill seen raising coffee exports.
newsitem.headline: Brazil tax bill seen raising coffee exports.

text.p: Last week's approval of a bill exempting Brazilian exports and capital goods from a heavy tax would boost the country's coffee exports, said Luiz Marcos Suplicy Hafers of the National Coffee Council of Brazil.
"We want to improve the share of Brazilian coffee in the world market, that is one of our objectives and it will happen," he told Reuters during the F.O. Licht world coffee conference here.
"Growers fought this tax for a long time and to our surprise the government lifted it. It will increase our competitiveness...the whole commodity sector feels like this," Hafers said.
"Negative opinions were expressed by state governors who lost revenue but the federal government supported the scheme," he continued.
The government on Sept 12 also cut surcharges on port tariffs, which is expected to help the flow of exports.
Hafers dismissed the idea that more exports would raise prices for domestic roasters.
"The domestic market is already linked closely to the level of exports," he said.
